t.E337.agn: According to EFSA, animal studies showed no toxic effects, including effects on the kidney, and no genotoxic potential. In 2020 EFSA set a group ADI for E 334–337 and E 354 of 240 mg/kg body weight per day, expressed as tartaric acid (replacing the SCF's 1990 ADI of 30 mg/kg), and stated that estimated exposure did not exceed this limit in any age group.
t.E337.body: Absorption of L(+)-tartaric acid is lower in humans than in rats.
t.E337.found.1: Fine bakery wares such as cakes and biscuits
t.E337.prod: Obtained by neutralising tartar from wine lees with sodium hydroxide or sodium carbonate and purifying it.
t.E337.regx.0: Re-evaluated; group ADI for E 334–337 and E 354 of 240 mg/kg body weight per day (as tartaric acid); exposure does not exceed the ADI.
t.E337.regx.1: Removed from Group I by 2024/1451; maximum levels by food category within the 'tartaric acid–tartrates' group (e.g. confectionery 25,000 mg/kg, fine bakery wares 18,000 mg/kg); applies from 16.12.2024.
t.E337.regx.2: ADI 0–30 mg/kg body weight (as L(+)-tartaric acid).
t.E337.summary: The sodium potassium salt of tartaric acid (Rochelle salt). Used as an acidity regulator.
t.E337.what: The sodium potassium salt of tartaric acid; it regulates the acidity of food.
